newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian shares end firmer despite Olivetti worries.
newsitem.headline: Italian shares end firmer despite Olivetti worries.

text.p: Italian stocks closed firmer on Friday with banks and telecoms leading the recovery despite continuing worries over Olivetti's financial accounts which the troubled information technology group has yet to clarify, traders said.

"The rise in Btp bond futures and the lira are helping equities which have seen a fair bit of short-covering," one dealer said. But the market remained nervous over what may yet emerge on Olivetti. An expected statement on its financial accounts had not been issued by the bourse session close.
The all-share Mibtel index closed up 1.16 pct at 9,393 and the Mib30 blue chip index ended 1.44 pct higher at 13,965.
"Monday could be a risky session," one trader said. "We could go up on a technical correction or fall if news on Olivetti is negative."

Merchant bank Mediobanca rose on market talk the bank would not come to the rescue of Olivetti whose shares remain suspended. Mediobanca closed up 2.73 percent at 8,115 lire. Banca di Roma ended 5.47 percent up at 1,118 after forecasting first half profit above that of the same period last year.
Telecoms were firm, with Telecom Italia up 2.51 percent at 2,935, mobile phone operator TIM up 2.48 percent at 3,055 and Stet holding company up 1.68 percent at 4,835 lire.

Two of Italy's largest banks, San Paolo and Banca Commerciale Italiana were cautious on their debt exposure to Olivetti, putting out statements denying figures published in Italian newspapers on their loans to the loss-making group.

Fiat ended 1.73 percent firmer at 4,522 lire, Montedison was up 1.7 percent at 957.3 and Pirelli edged up 0.48 percent to 2,537 but energy group Eni, facing a second tranche of its privatisation in October, slipped 0.12 percent to 6,537 lire.
